verses.text: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, appointed to strengthen the faith of God's chosen people and help them know the truth that leads to godliness,
and to give them hope of eternal life. God, who never lies, promised that life before time began.
At the right time, he revealed his message through the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior.
To Titus, my true child in our shared faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
I left you in Crete for this reason: to set right what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
An elder must be above reproach, faithful to one wife, and have children who believe and aren't known for wild or rebellious behavior.
An overseer, as God's steward, must be above reproach. They must not be arrogant, quick-tempered, addicted to wine, violent, or greedy for dishonest gain.
Instead, they should welcome guests, love what is good, be sensible, fair, holy, and self-controlled.
They must hold firmly to the trustworthy message as it was taught, so they can encourage others with sound teaching and correct those who oppose it.
There are many rebellious people, empty talkers, and deceivers, especially among those who insist on circumcision.
They must be silenced, because they are upsetting whole households by teaching what they shouldn't for dishonest profit.
One of their own prophets said, ‘Cretans are always liars, vicious beasts, and lazy gluttons.’
That statement is true. So correct them sharply, so they may become sound in the faith
and stop paying attention to Jewish myths and commands from people who turn away from the truth.
To the pure, everything is pure. But to those who are corrupted and don't believe, nothing is pure; both their minds and consciences are corrupted.
They claim to know God, but their actions deny him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
But teach what fits sound doctrine.
Teach older men to be clear-minded, dignified, and self-controlled, sound in faith, love, and endurance.
In the same way, teach older women to live reverently, not slander others or be controlled by too much wine. They should teach what is good,
so they can train younger women to love their husbands and children,
to be sensible and pure, care for their households, be kind, and submit to their husbands, so God's word won't be slandered.
In the same way, encourage younger men to be self-controlled.
In everything, show yourself as an example of good works. In your teaching, show integrity, dignity,
and sound speech that can't be condemned, so anyone who opposes you will have nothing bad to say about us.
Teach enslaved people to submit to their masters and try to please them in everything. They shouldn't talk back
or steal, but should show complete trustworthiness, so that in every way they make the teaching about God our Savior attractive.
God's grace has appeared, bringing salvation to all people.
It teaches us to reject godlessness and worldly desires, and to live with self-control, righteousness, and devotion to God in this present age,
as we wait for the blessed hope—the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
He gave himself for us to set us free from all wickedness and to make us pure, his own people, eager to do what is good.
Teach these things. Encourage and correct with full authority. Don't let anyone disregard you.
Remind people to submit to rulers and authorities, obey them, and be ready to do every good work.
They shouldn't slander anyone or be argumentative. They should be gentle and show consideration for everyone.
We too were once foolish, disobedient, and led astray. We were enslaved to all kinds of desires and pleasures. We lived with malice and envy, hating others and being hated.
But when God our Savior showed his kindness and love for humanity,
he saved us—not because of good things we had done, but because of his mercy. He saved us through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
whom he generously poured out on us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that by his grace we could be made right and become heirs with the hope of eternal life.
This saying is trustworthy. I want you to insist on these things, so those who have believed God will be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and helpful for everyone.
But avoid foolish arguments, family trees, quarrels, and disputes about the law. They're useless and pointless.
Warn a divisive person once, and then a second time. After that, have nothing more to do with them.
You know that such a person is twisted and keeps sinning, condemning themselves.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me in Nicopolis, because I've decided to spend the winter there.
Help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, and make sure they have everything they need.
Our people should learn to devote themselves to doing good, meeting urgent needs, so they won't live unproductive lives.
Everyone with me sends greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
